ddl: CREATE TABLE customer (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL, year INTEGER NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE book (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, year INTEGER NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE loan (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, book_id INTEGER NOT NULL, days INTEGER NOT NULL)

cases.question: How many customers are from Sweden?
cases.evidence: country holds the ISO country code.
cases.goldSql: SELECT count(*) FROM customer WHERE country = 'SE'

cases.question: List every customer name.
cases.evidence: name is the customer's display name.

cases.question: How many orders are there?
cases.evidence: One row per order, whatever its value.

cases.question: How many loans lasted more than 10 days?
cases.evidence: days is the loan length in whole days.
cases.goldSql: SELECT count(*) FROM loan WHERE days > 10
